messages:
alex: Customer reports inconsistent tool_result association when making parallel tool calls via the function-calling API. Payload had two tools called in parallel and the response mixed up results between tool ids. Correlation-id: cid=0x9f4a7e. Sample request below. We've got a reproducible trace and minimal repro. Can we triage?

maria: Thanks Alex — can you paste the request body + headers and any gateway request-id? Also the client concurrency / batch settings you used.

alex: Here: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' 
  -H 'X-Correlation-Id: 0x9f4a7e' 
  -H 'X-Request-Id: r-8402' 
  -d '{
    "input": "Summarize and then fetch metadata",
    "tools": [
      {"id": "summarize_v1", "call": {"prompt": "..."}},
      {"id": "fetch_meta_v2", "call": {"resource": "/items/123"}}
    ],
    "parallel": true
  }'

  Response (excerpt):
  {
    "tool_results": [
      {"tool_id":"fetch_meta_v2","result_id":"tr-77","output":{...}},
      {"tool_id":"summarize_v1","result_id":"tr-78","output":{...}}
    ],
    "model_output": "... uses summary from tr-78 but associates it with tr-77 ..."
  }

  Logs: 
  [runtime] INFO route=call request_id=r-8402 correlation=0x9f4a7e dispatch=fanout(2)
  [runtime] DEBUG fanout_id=fan-992 schedule: summon worker(10), worker(11)
  [worker-10] DEBUG tool_call start tool=summarize_v1 call_id=call-77
  [worker-11] DEBUG tool_call start tool=fetch_meta_v2 call_id=call-78
  [worker-11] DEBUG tool_call finish call_id=call-78 result_id=tr-77
  [worker-10] DEBUG tool_call finish call_id=call-77 result_id=tr-78

  Notice the result_id assignment doesn't match call_id ordering.

support-eng: Can you re-run with DEBUG_HTTP=1 and attach the full gateway logs and the JSON we can replay? Also include SDK version.

maria: Also include the fanout_id header if possible. If this is happening only under high parallelism that hints at a pool-level ID reuse or race in the result->call mapping.

jordan: I skimmed the runtime logs — it looks like result_id allocations are coming from a shared counter that may be assigned on write completion without atomically tying to the call_id. Potential race: two workers finish close together and the mappings to the original call slots get swapped when merged into the fanout response.

sre-bot: Deploy info: runtime@prod-3 deployed 2026-03-15T02:10:12Z (sha: b7c2f1). No incidents triggered.

alex: Repro steps: set parallel=true, concurrency=2, SDK v0.9.8, send 200 short requests hitting both tools in same payload. Fail rate ~2%. Attaching a tiny repro script (will paste below).

support-eng: Please attach replayable payload. If we can repro locally we can hotpatch.

alex: Repro script snippet: 
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'X-Correlation-Id: 0x9f4a7e' -d '{"input":"x","tools":[{"id":"t1","call":{}},{"id":"t2","call":{}}],"parallel":true}' &
  done; wait

maria: Suggested short-term workaround: set parallel=false for multi-tool payloads or add per-tool explicit call_id in the args that the server will echo back, so the client can re-associate if mismatch occurs. We'll roll a note in the SDK docs.

jordan: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to add an atomic mapping when merging fanout results (priority: high). 2) support to collect all failing request_ids + traces (r-8402, r-8409, r-8421 etc.). 3) consider feature flag to serialize result_id allocation.

support-eng: Escalating to eng-runtime oncall @jordan, marking P1 for customer-impacting misassociation. Adding ticket INF-4521 with logs.

alex: One more data point — billing query: customer saw tokens charged for both tools even when one output was apparently used twice. Could be double-counting at aggregation step. Please check billing pipeline.

jordan: Noted. I'll also check the aggregator that tallies token usage per tool_result to ensure result_id uniqueness.

maria: Assigning owners: eng-runtime=jordan, support=alex, tooling=support-eng. Will follow up with ETA after initial debugging. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks — I'll attach the full traces (gateway + runtime) in a thread thread and post the replayable JSON.

support-eng: Keeping thread open until fix or reliable mitigation deployed.
